items.question_text: You manage a Google Cloud project that contains a critical marketing application. You need to grant an external vendor read-only access to the objects stored in a specific Cloud Storage bucket. The vendor must not be able to view any other resources in the project. What should you do?

choices.text: Create a custom IAM role with the storage.objects.get permission, and grant the vendor this role on the project.
Grant the vendor the Storage Object User role on the project.
Grant the vendor the Storage Object User role on the bucket.
Grant the vendor the Storage Object Viewer role on the bucket.

items.question_text: You manage IAM policies for your organization’s Google Cloud project. A new operations team needs the capability to start, stop, and reset existing Compute Engine VM instances within this project for basic troubleshooting. Due to strict security requirements, the operations team must be prevented from deleting any instances or modifying any networking or configuration settings. You need to grant the minimum necessary permissions to the team members. What should you do?
items.solution_text: The question explicitly requires granting the *minimum necessary permissions*, which is achieved by creating a custom IAM role containing only the specific permissions for starting, stopping, and resetting instances. Predefined roles like `compute.instanceAdmin.v1` (Option B) are too permissive as they include delete and modify capabilities, even if conditions were applied, while Option A grants excessive write access and Option D lacks execution permissions entirely.

choices.text: Grant the operations team the roles/writer IAM role, and add the resource.type =='compute.googleapis.com/Instance' condition to the role.
Grant the operations team the predefined roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1 IAM role on the project. Apply an IAM condition to exclude the compute.instances.delete permission.
Create a custom IAM role that includes only the compute.instances.start, compute.instances.stop, and compute.instances.reset permissions. Assign this role to the operations team on the project.

Grant the operations team the predefined roles/compute.viewer IAM role to allow them to view the instances. Instruct them to use the Google Cloud Console’s basic actions such as starting, stopping, and resetting.

items.question_text: You are conducting an audit of your Google Cloud organization. You need to identify all Compute Engine instances that have a public IP address. You want to implement a solution that is easy to maintain and uses Google Cloud managed services. What should you do?

choices.text: Enable the compute.vmExternalIpAccess organization policy at the organization level.
Use Cloud Shell and Gemini CLI to query the Compute Engine API for instances with a public IP address.
Use Cloud Asset Inventory to query for all Compute Engine instances with a public IP address.
Create a shell script using the gcloud CLI to find all instances with a public IP address.

items.question_text: You are responsible for Google Cloud governance at your company and recently implemented a new, automated process for provisioning Google Cloud projects. You have discovered several projects that were manually created before the implementation of this new process. You need to identify the creators of these projects to inform them of the new process. What should you do?
items.solution_text: Every Google Cloud project must have at least one user with the Owner IAM role. By reviewing the IAM page in the console, you can identify these owners and contact them regarding the new provisioning process.

choices.text: Review the value of the creator label attached to the project to find the project’s creator.
Use Resource Manager to identify the responsible department from the folder and project hierarchy.
Review the Cloud Billing account linked to the project, and then contact the owner of that billing account.
Use the IAM page in the Google Cloud console to identify the user with the Owner role.
